description:
In dkim.rs::has_dkim_signature_header, the header_end computation is: article_bytes.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"\r\n\r\n").or_else(|| article_bytes.windows(2).position(|w| w == b"\n\n")). When no CRLF-CRLF is found, the or_else fallback scans article_bytes.windows(2) for 

. But article_bytes.windows(2) scans the ENTIRE article from byte 0, not from where the CRLF-CRLF scan left off. For an article using CRLF line endings with no separator yet (truncated), this means the 

 scan will find the first 

 in any CRLF pair within the article body -- e.g. the 
 sequences include 
 bytes, and two consecutive 

 would have adjacent 
 bytes at offsets n and n+2 (not adjacent), but a bare 

 in the body would be found. Crucially, if found, the position points into the body, and header_bytes = &article_bytes[..header_end] would include body content, allowing a DKIM-Signature: line in the body to be detected as a header. The existing test 'DKIM-Signature: in body must not be detected' passes only because the test uses 

 as the separator, so the 

 path fires first. A test with a mixed separator (CRLF headers, no separator, DKIM-Signature in body followed by 

) would fail.
title: sieve-native: DKIM header check or_else for \n\n search starts fresh scan from byte 0
